questions.q: What are the five layers of this capstone's architecture, in order?
options: Power BI, dbt, Python, Snowflake, CI/CD
Snowflake, dbt, Python ingestion, CI/CD, Power BI
dbt, Snowflake, CI/CD, Power BI, Python ingestion
CI/CD, Snowflake, dbt, Power BI, Python ingestion
questions.explain: Snowflake first (compute/storage/access), then dbt (transformation), then Python ingestion, then the CI/CD gate, then Power BI on top.

questions.q: Why can't dbt alone load a one-off CSV from an external system with no native Snowflake connector?
options: dbt transforms data already inside Snowflake — it doesn't load external files into Snowflake in the first place, which is a separate ingestion job
dbt is not allowed to run SELECT statements on external data
Snowflake doesn't support CSV files under any circumstances
dbt can only read from Python scripts, never from raw tables
questions.explain: dbt's job starts once data is already in Snowflake; getting a new external source into Snowflake in the first place is what the Python ingestion layer is for.

questions.q: Why does Power BI connect only to the PROD schema's marts, never RAW or DEV?
options: Power BI is technically incapable of connecting to any other schema
Because PROD contains only marts that have already passed dbt's tests and the CI/CD gate — it's a deliberate governance boundary, not an afterthought
RAW and DEV schemas don't exist in Snowflake
Because Snowflake charges extra for BI tools connecting to RAW
questions.explain: Restricting the BI connection to PROD is itself a governance control — it guarantees business users only ever see data that has cleared every check.

questions.q: Why does the order of these five layers matter, rather than building them in any sequence?
options: The order is arbitrary and doesn't matter at all
Each layer is load-bearing for the next — dbt needs a role and schema from Snowflake, CI/CD needs real models and tests to run dbt build against, and so on
Snowflake must always be built last for security reasons
Power BI must be connected before any data exists, so it can validate the schema in advance
questions.explain: Each layer depends on something concrete the previous layer produced — skipping ahead leaves the next layer with nothing real to stand on.

questions.q: What is the TRANSFORMER role's job in this architecture, as planned in this lesson?
options: It's the role Power BI connects as to read PROD marts
It's the Snowflake role dbt runs as — able to read RAW and write to DEV/PROD
It's a Python library used for data cleaning
It's the GitHub Actions role used to approve pull requests
questions.explain: TRANSFORMER is the role dbt itself runs as, scoped to read raw data and write the models it builds — distinct from the read-only ANALYST role Power BI uses.
